method_card.title: Weather, Travel Problems and Transactions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers German weather expressions, travel problem language, and transactional phrases for tourist information — including the important kein vs nicht distinction for complaints.

GermanEnglish
Es ist sonnig.It is sunny.
Es ist heiß / warm / kalt.It is hot / warm / cold.
Es ist schön / schlecht.It is nice / bad (weather).
Es ist bewölkt / windig / neblig.It is cloudy / windy / foggy.
Es regnet.It is raining.
Es schneit.It is snowing.
die Temperaturtemperature
der Sonnenscheinsunshine
die Touristeninformationtourist information office
der Stadtplantown map / street map
der Zug hat Verspätung.The train is delayed.
Ich habe meinen Pass verloren.I have lost my passport.
Mein Gepäck ist weg.My luggage is gone / missing.

Grammar focus — weather expressions: Use es ist + adjective for weather states: Es ist sonnig, Es ist kalt, Es ist bewölkt. Use es + verb for precipitation: Es regnet, Es schneit, Es donnert. Past: change ist to war: Es war sonnig. Future: Es wird regnen (werden + infinitive at end).

Grammar focus — kein vs nicht in complaints: kein negates a noun phrase: Ich habe kein Gepäck (I have no luggage — noun without article → kein). nicht negates verbs, adjectives and definite noun phrases: Der Zug kommt nicht (the train isn't coming — verb); Das Gepäck ist nicht hier (the luggage is not here — adjective/location). Common exam error: Ich habe nicht Gepäck is wrong — it should be kein Gepäck.

Grammar focus — als vs wenn: als = single past event: Als es regnete, sind wir ins Museum gegangen. wenn = repeated events or present/future conditions: Wenn es regnet, gehe ich nicht zur Touristeninformation. Both send the verb to the end.

Model paragraph: Als wir ankamen, war das Wetter schlecht — es hat geregnet und es war kalt. Deshalb sind wir zur Touristeninformation gegangen und haben einen Stadtplan bekommen. Wenn es morgen schön ist, werden wir die Sehenswürdigkeiten besichtigen. (When we arrived, the weather was bad — it was raining and cold. So we went to the tourist information office and got a town map. If it is nice tomorrow, we will visit the sights.)
steps: Learn weather expressions: es ist + adjective (sonnig, kalt) vs es + verb (regnet, schneit)
Master the kein vs nicht distinction: kein for noun negation, nicht for verb/adjective negation
Distinguish als (single past event) from wenn (repeated / present / future condition) — both send verb to end
Build tourist-information-office role-play responses using Sie register and polite request forms

exam_context.frequency: High-frequency topic — weather links to holidays, activities and the picture-card task; tourist information is a prescribed role-play setting

worked_examples.question: What does 'Es war sonnig und heiß' mean?

steps.label: Identify the verb
steps.content: war = was (preterite of sein). This tells us we are describing past weather.

steps.label: Translate the adjectives
steps.content: sonnig = sunny, heiß = hot. Both are predicative — no adjective ending needed.

worked_examples.question: Translate: 'Because it rained, we went to the museum.' — and explain the word order.

steps.label: Subordinate clause with weil
steps.content: weil sends the verb to the end: 'it rained' → es geregnet hat. Full clause: weil es geregnet hat.

steps.label: Main clause after weil-clause
steps.content: When the weil-clause comes first, the main clause verb inverts: verb at position 2 immediately after the comma. 'We went' = sind wir gegangen (sein — movement verb gehen). ins Museum = in das → ins (neuter accusative, motion).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Weil es geregnet hat, sind wir ins Museum gegangen.

bronze.question: Match the German to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct past weather verb

gaps.rule: Preterite of sein — verb-final after weil
gaps.correct_explain: war is the preterite of sein. After weil, the verb goes to the end of the clause.

wrong.ist: ist is present tense. The sentence describes the past — use war.
wrong.waren: waren is the wir/sie plural form. The subject is es (it) — use war.

gaps.rule: Past participle of gehen — takes sein
gaps.correct_explain: gegangen is the past participle of gehen (to go). It takes sein as auxiliary.

wrong.geht: geht is present tense. You need the past participle: gegangen.
wrong.gehen: gehen is the infinitive. You need the past participle: gegangen.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct negation

gaps.correct_explain: geregnet is the past participle of regnen (to rain). Es hat geregnet = it rained.

wrong.regnet: regnet is present tense. With hat, you need the past participle: geregnet.

gaps.rule: Past participle of bleiben — state-change, takes sein
gaps.correct_explain: geblieben is the past participle of bleiben (to stay). Bleiben is a state-change verb — it takes sein: sind wir geblieben.

wrong.gebleibt: There is no form gebleibt. Bleiben is irregular: geblieben.

bronze.question: What does 'Als es kalt war, sind wir im Hotel geblieben' mean?
options: When it was cold, we stayed in the hotel
Because it is cold, we are staying in the hotel
If it was cold, we went to the hotel
Although it was cold, we left the hotel

bronze.question: Which sentence is correct? (kein vs nicht)

bronze.source_text: Letzten Sommer war das Wetter fantastisch. Wir haben am Strand gelegen und Fotos gemacht.
model_answers: Last summer the weather was fantastic. We lay on the beach and took photos.
hints: am Strand gelegen = lay on the beach

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear

bronze.correct_text: Es war sonnig und sehr heiß.
bronze.translation: It was sunny and very hot.

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: **When** I was on holiday, it **snowed** every day.
sentence_parts: ich im Urlaub war, hat es jeden Tag

gaps.correct_explain: Als is used for a single event in the past. Wenn would mean 'whenever' (repeated) or be used for present/future conditions.

wrong.Wenn: Wenn is for repeated events or present/future conditions. For a single past event, use als.

gaps.correct_explain: geschneit is the past participle of schneien (to snow). Es hat geschneit = it snowed.

wrong.schneit: schneit is present tense. With hat, you need the past participle: geschneit.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ich habe nicht Gepäck — es ist verloren gegangen.
silver.explanation: Gepäck is a noun without an article here. Use kein to negate a noun phrase (kein = not a / no). nicht negates verbs and adjectives, not bare nouns.
silver.translation: I have no luggage — it has gone missing.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: It rained, therefore we went to the museum.

distractor_labels.haben: wrong auxiliary — gehen is a movement verb and takes sein, not haben.

silver.source_text: The train is delayed and there are no tickets. Can you help me?
model_answers: Der Zug hat Verspätung und es gibt keine Fahrkarten. Können Sie mir helfen?

Check: der Zug hat Verspätung (idiom — use haben, not sein); kein/keine for noun negation (keine Fahrkarten — plural keine); formal register Können Sie; modal + infinitive at end (Können Sie mir helfen). silver.question: Listen and type what you hear
silver.audio_text: Wenn es morgen schön ist, werde ich die Sehenswürdigkeiten besichtigen.
silver.correct_text: Wenn es morgen schön ist, werde ich die Sehenswürdigkeiten besichtigen.
silver.translation: If it is nice tomorrow, I will visit the tourist sights.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: When we were in Spain, the weather was fantastic. We swam in the sea every day and visited many tourist sights. If it rains next time, we will go to an indoor museum.
model_answers: Als wir in Spanien waren, war das Wetter fantastisch. Wir sind jeden Tag im Meer geschwommen und haben viele Sehenswürdigkeiten besucht. Wenn es nächstes Mal regnet, werden wir in ein Museum gehen.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a translation from English to German. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: als vs wenn distinction (als for single past event in Spain; wenn for future conditional), verb-final in both subordinate clauses, sein for schwimmen (movement), haben for besuchen (transitive, no ge- on besucht because of inseparable be-), werden + infinitive for future (gehen at end). Accept valid alternatives. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: Because the weather was bad, we stayed in the hotel.

distractor_labels.ist,: wrong tense — describing the past. Use war (preterite), not ist (present).
distractor_labels.haben: wrong auxiliary — bleiben is a state-change verb and takes sein, not haben.
distractor_labels.bleiben: wrong form — you need the past participle geblieben, not the infinitive.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a tourist information office in a German town. You need help with information and a travel problem.

bullets.prompt: Greet the member of staff and ask for a town map and a list of local sights.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Tag! Könnten Sie mir bitte einen Stadtplan und eine Liste der Sehenswürdigkeiten geben?
bullets.note: formal greeting; Könnten Sie (polite Konjunktiv II); einen Stadtplan (masculine accusative); eine Liste (feminine accusative)

bullets.prompt: Ask what the weather will be like tomorrow.
bullets.model_answer: Wie wird das Wetter morgen sein?
bullets.note: werden + infinitive for future (sein at end after morgen); Wie (question word)

bullets.prompt: Report that your train is delayed and ask which platform you need.
bullets.model_answer: Mein Zug hat Verspätung. Von welchem Bahnsteig fährt er ab?
bullets.note: hat Verspätung (idiom); von welchem Bahnsteig (dative after von); abfahren separable — fährt … ab

bullets.prompt: Say the weather was bad yesterday so you could not do any sightseeing.
bullets.model_answer: Gestern war das Wetter schlecht, deshalb konnte ich keine Sehenswürdigkeiten besichtigen.
bullets.note: war (preterite); deshalb (therefore — conjunctional adverb, verb still at position 2 in next clause: konnte ich); konnte (simple past of können — Foundation: ich konnte); keine (noun negation, plural)

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a role play set at a tourist information office. The student must use Sie register throughout. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the German grammatically accurate? Check: Könnten Sie (polite Konjunktiv II), werden + infinitive for weather forecast, hat Verspätung (correct idiom), kein/keine for noun negation, separable verb abfahren (prefix at end in main clause). Award marks out of 10. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about a holiday where the weather caused problems. Include: what the weather was like, what you did as a result, a travel problem you experienced, and what you will do differently next time.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about weather and travel problems. Mark on: Communication (all four bullet points addressed?), Range of language (weather expressions es ist/war + adjective and es regnet/regnet, als or wenn with verb-final, perfect tense with sein and haben, kein vs nicht for negation, future with werden + infinitive or conditional würde), Accuracy (verb-second rule after time/place phrases, verb-final in subordinate clauses after weil/als/wenn, noun capitalisation, correct past participles, kein agreement). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.audio_text: Als wir in Spanien waren, war das Wetter fantastisch, und wir haben jeden Tag am Strand gelegen.
gold.correct_text: Als wir in Spanien waren, war das Wetter fantastisch, und wir haben jeden Tag am Strand gelegen.
gold.translation: When we were in Spain, the weather was fantastic, and we lay on the beach every day.

gold.source_text: Despite the bad weather, the holiday was wonderful. I would go back because the people were so friendly.
model_answers: Trotz des schlechten Wetters war der Urlaub wunderbar. Ich würde wieder hinfahren, weil die Menschen so freundlich waren.
